requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL server installed on node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: postgresql-server/contrib 16.14 installed and rpm-verified on all three nodes; node2's initial install failed on a transient GPG-key parse error and was successfully retried.

requirements.requirement: node1 configured as writable streaming-replication primary
requirements.summary: initdb run on node1, replicator role created, postgresql.conf set wal_level=replica/max_wal_senders/max_replication_slots/hot_standby, pg_hba.conf opened scram-sha-256 replication access for node2/node3, service restarted and confirmed active with the new settings applied.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys streaming from node1
requirements.summary: Dedicated physical replication slots created on the primary; pg_basebackup -R cloned the primary onto both standbys (standby.signal + primary_conninfo present); both standbys started and pg_stat_replication on the primary shows both walreceivers in streaming/async state; INSERT attempts on both standbys were rejected with a read-only-transaction error.

requirements.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
requirements.summary: A table was created and rows inserted on node1; both standbys immediately showed the identical rows via SELECT. This was re-verified after a full restart cycle, when a new row inserted on the restarted primary also replicated to both standbys.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: node1 was configured as a writable primary, node2 and node3 were built as read-only physical standbys via pg_basebackup with dedicated replication slots and confirmed streaming, standby writes were shown to be rejected, and primary writes were shown to propagate to both standbys both before and after a full one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed thoroughly: pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, boot-identity changes, and post-restart recovery/replication/data checks were captured for node2, node3, and node1 (primary), and the observed boot IDs match the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot exactly, corroborating the trace.
limitations: Evidence for standby read-only/streaming state and data visibility relies on psql output captured shortly after actions; no long-duration steady-state monitoring was captured, though this is not required by the task.
The prepare phase was disabled (after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare), so all observed state changes are attributable to the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands map cleanly to task steps (install, initdb, role/config, slots, basebackup, verification). Two bounded self-corrected mutations occurred: an initial openssl-based password generation failed (openssl absent) and was immediately replaced with a working urandom-based generator (cmd-2135debd7ec34bc3 -> cmd-6568c33047f54f97); and pg_basebackup on node2/node3 was first invoked with a redundant -C flag that collided with the already-created slots and auto-wiped the target data directory before a corrected retry succeeded (cmd-833a9afd0d184228, cmd-b1e3e32dd06947c9 -> cmd-535d97b1d44e4183/cmd-3a3ba3f9e35b4cf5). Neither left residue: the plaintext replication-password files were explicitly removed on all three nodes (cmd-2629cf4a4c834a7d, cmd-9b1e3329dd8c4739, cmd-71ba2da44b0c4283) after use. Cluster-wide passwordless SSH and firewalld postgresql exposure were opened, which are reasonable, bounded prerequisites for password transfer and inter-node replication traffic rather than unnecessary changes. Post-executor snapshots show no failed services and no unexplained residue beyond expected install/reboot log files.
